transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. What brings you in to see me today?

I came in because I’ve been trying to make my art into a freelance business, and it’s been getting to me more than I expected. I get really wound up about invoices or client messages, then I avoid dealing with them. Sometimes I end up crying at my kitchen table, or I forget normal things like paying a bill.
When did you first start noticing this worry, crying, and forgetfulness—did it begin around the time you started the freelance business, and how long has it been going on since then?
Yeah, it started about a month ago, when I began trying to make my art into a more formal freelance business. It’s been going on since then.
Over this past month, have you been feeling down, sad, or uninterested in things you used to enjoy on most days, even when you're not dealing with the business stuff?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed that being an all-the-time thing outside of the business stuff.
Aside from the freelance business worries, do you find yourself excessively worrying about other things in your life, like health, relationships, or other responsibilities?
No, I don’t think so. It’s mostly centered on the freelance business and everything that comes with that.
Besides the worry and crying, have you noticed feeling persistently down, hopeless, or low in mood specifically about this business situation, separate from the anxious feelings?

Yeah, I do get pretty low about it sometimes. I’ll get so wound up over an invoice or a client message that I just avoid it, and then I end up crying at my kitchen table. It feels like I can’t handle normal business things.

Has this stress been affecting other areas of your life—like your relationships, sleep, or your ability to handle daily responsibilities outside of the business—or does it stay pretty contained to the business tasks?

It’s started to spill over some. I’ve put off replying to clients, and I missed a utility payment because I was trying to keep up with the art display and everything else. Home responsibilities are harder to stay on top of.

final_diagnosis.reason: Symptoms of anxiety (worry, avoidance) and depressed mood (crying, feeling low, sense of inadequacy) emerged within one month of a clearly identifiable psychosocial stressor (transitioning art into a freelance business). Symptoms are disproportionate to the stressor, causing functional impairment (missed bill payment, avoidance of client communication, difficulty with home responsibilities), but do not meet full criteria for GAD (worry is restricted to the business domain rather than multiple life areas) or Major Depressive Disorder (low mood is not pervasive or present most days independent of the stressor). This pattern of mixed anxious and depressive symptoms tied temporally and thematically to an identifiable stressor is most consistent with Adjustment Disorder with mixed anxiety and depressed mood.
